{{short description|Italian astroparticle physicist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=December 2024}}
'''Elisa Resconi''' (born 1 December 1971 in [[Brescia]], Italy) is an  Italian [[Astroparticle physics|astroparticle physicist]] and the Chair of [[Experimental Physics]] with Cosmic Particles at the [[Technical University of Munich]], [[Germany]]. Her research concentrates on high-energy [[neutrino astronomy]] and developing advanced detection technologies for [[cosmic particle]]s.<ref name="TUMresconi">{{cite web|url=https://www.professoren.tum.de/en/resconi-elisa|title=Prof. Dr. Elisa Resconi|publisher=[[Technical University of Munich]]|accessdate=14 January 2025}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
From 1989 to 1995, Resconi studied physics at the [[University of Milan]]. She earned her PhD from the [[University of Genoa]] in 2001 under the supervision of G. Manuzio and R. Raghavan. From 2002 to 2005, she worked as a [[Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions|Marie Curie Postdoctoral Fellow]] at [[DESY]] Zeuthen, Germany, and from 2005 to 2011, she led an [[Emmy Noether Program|Emmy Noether research group]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics]] in [[Heidelberg]], Germany.<ref name="DFGresconi">{{cite web|url=https://gepris-extern.dfg.de/gepris/OCTOPUS?beginOfFunding=&bewilligungsStatus=&context=projekt&continentId=%23&countryKey=%23%23%23&einrichtungsart=-1&fachlicheZuordnung=%23&findButton=historyCall&gefoerdertIn=&hitsPerPage=10&index=0&keywords_criterion=&location=&nurProjekteMitAB=false&oldContinentId=%23&oldCountryId=%23%23%23&oldSubContinentId=%23%23&orderBy=gz&pemu=%23&person=Resconi%2C+Elisa&subContinentId=%23%23&task=doSearchExtended&teilprojekte=false&zk_transferprojekt=false|title=Elisa Resconi DFG Funded Projects|publisher=[[German Research Foundation]]|accessdate=28 November 2024}}</ref> After serving as a guest professor at the [[University of Erlangen–Nuremberg|University of Erlangen-Nuremberg]] in 2011, she moved to the Technical University of Munich (TUM) and held a Heisenberg Professorship from 2013 to 2016. In 2018, she was appointed Liesel Beckmann Distinguished Professor for [[Experimental physics]] at TUM.<ref name="TUMresconi">{{cite web|url=https://www.professoren.tum.de/en/resconi-elisa|title=Prof. Dr. Elisa Resconi|publisher=[[Technical University of Munich]]|accessdate=14 January 2025}}</ref>

Since 2017, Resconi has been the spokesperson of the [[German Research Foundation|DFG]] [[Collaborative Research Center]] 1258 (SFB1258) "[[Neutrino]]s and [[Dark Matter]] in [[Astrophysics]] and [[Particle Physics]]".<ref name="DFGresconi"/><ref name="TUM-20161123">{{cite news |title=New Collaborative Research Center at the TUM == Research ==
Elisa Resconi's research is focused on the detection and analysis of high-energy neutrinos, elementary particles that offer insights into the universe's most energetic astrophysical phenomena. As a member of the [[IceCube Neutrino Observatory|IceCube Collaboration]], she has been particularly involved in studies linking neutrino emissions to the AGN [[NGC 1068]], a nearby [[Seyfert galaxy]]. This discovery provides critical evidence for AGN as potential sources of high-energy cosmic neutrinos and highlights the role of neutrinos in understanding the universe's most extreme environments.<ref name="GT-20221104">{{cite news |title=IceCube Neutrinos Give Us First Glimpse Into the Inner Depths of an Active Galaxy  |url=https://research.gatech.edu/icecube-neutrinos-give-us-first-glimpse-inner-depths-active-galaxy |date=4 November 2022 |publisher=[[Georgia Tech]] |access-date=14 January 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Abbasi |first1=R. |last2=Ackermann |first2=M. |last3=Adams |first3=J. |last4=Aguilar |first4=J. == The Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment (P-ONE) ==
Resconi's recent work centers on the [[Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment]] (P-ONE), an international collaboration to establish a large-scale neutrino observatory in the Pacific Ocean. The experiment seeks to deploy an array of detectors at great depths to capture high-energy neutrinos with unprecedented precision using the subsea infrastructure of the NEPTUNE observatory of [[Ocean Networks Canada]] (ONC).<ref name="ST-20180730">{{cite news |title=Ocean Networks Canada installs neutrino detector in deep pacific |url=https://sea-technology.com/ocean-networks-canada-installs-neutrino-detector-in-deep-pacific |date=30 July 2018 |publisher=Sea Technology |access-date=14 January 2025 }}</ref><ref name="ONC-20230824">{{cite news |title=Studying the origins of the universe, under the sea |url=https://www.oceannetworks.ca/news-and-stories/stories/studying-the-origins-of-the-universe-under-the-sea/ |date=24 August 2023 |publisher=[[Ocean Networks Canada]] |access-date=14 January 2025 }}</ref> P-ONE aims at addressing key unanswered questions in [[astrophysics]], such as the origin of [[cosmic ray]]s and the properties of [[dark matter]].<ref name=Johnson-Groh>{{cite web|author=Johnson-Groh, Mara|url=https://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/proposed-experiment-seeks-origin-of-cosmic-neutrinos? |title=Proposed experiment seeks origin of cosmic neutrinos |date=31 January 2023|website=Symmetry Magazine|accessdate=14 January 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Agostini |first1=Matteo |last2=Böhmer |first2=Michael |last3=Bosma |first3=Jeff |last4=Clark |first4=Kenneth |last5=Danninger |first5=Matthias |last6=Fruck |first6=Christian |last7=Gernhäuser |first7=Roman |last8=Gärtner |first8=Andreas |last9=Grant |first9=Darren |last10=Henningsen |first10=Felix |last11=Holzapfel |first11=Kilian |last12=Huber |first12=Matthias |last13=Jenkyns |first13=Reyna |last14=Krauss |first14=Carsten B. |last15=Krings |first15=Kai |last16=Kopper |first16=Claudio |last17=Leismüller |first17=Klaus |last18=Leys |first18=Sally |last19=Macoun |first19=Paul |last20=Meighen-Berger |first20=Stephan |last21=Michel |first21=Jan |last22=Moore |first22=Roger |last23=Morley |first23=Mike |last24=Padovani |first24=Paolo |last25=Papp |first25=Laszlo |last26=Pirenne |first26=Benoit |last27=Qiu |first27=Chuantao |last28=Rea |first28=Immacolata Carmen |last29=Resconi |first29=Elisa |last30=Round |first30=Adrian |last31=Ruskey |first31=Albert |last32=Spannfellner |first32=Christian |last33=Traxler |first33=Michael |last34=Turcati |first34=Andrea |last35=Yanez |first35=Juan Pablo |title=The Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment |journal=Nature Astronomy |date=8 September 2020 |volume=4 |issue=10 |pages=913–915 |doi=10.1038/s41550-020-1182-4 |arxiv=2005.09493 |bibcode=2020NatAs...4..913A }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Malecki |first1=Paweł |title=Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment |journal=Universe |date=23 January 2024 |volume=10 |issue=2 |pages=53 |doi=10.3390/universe10020053 |doi-access=free |bibcode=2024Univ...10...53M }}</ref>
